quickAnswer: To compare 3 quotes for commercial office cleaning accurately, divide each bidder's monthly flat fee by 4.33 weeks per month and their committed weekly labor hours to reveal the true hourly bill rate, which should benchmark between $35 and $65 per hour nationally. For standard multi-tenant offices between 2,500 and 24,999 square feet, normalized base pricing typically falls between $0.07 and $0.15 per cleanable square foot per visit before adding $15 to $30 per restroom or $0.012 to $0.025 per square foot for paper and soap consumables.

blocks.text: Why Three Janitorial Bids Rarely Line Up on the First Pass

Corporate procurement policies almost universally mandate a three-bid tender before awarding or renewing a commercial janitorial service agreement. However, when three local building service contractors (BSCs) walk the same 15,000-square-foot suite and submit proposals ranging from $2,400 to $4,350 per month, the price spread rarely reflects pure profit margin variance. Instead, the spread stems from unaligned assumptions around cleanable square footage, production rates per labor hour, restroom fixture density, and whether periodic floor care or restroom consumables are bundled into the monthly retainer.

A disciplined comparison requires stripping away marketing brochures and decomposing every quote into four auditable denominators: cleanable square footage (excluding mechanical rooms, vertical penetrations, and locked storage), monthly visit multiplier (using the standard 4.33 weeks per month rather than a 4.0-week shorthand), allocated nightly man-hours based on the ISSA 3,500 square feet per hour general office production benchmark, and line-itemized pass-through costs for paper, soap, and can liners.

blocks.title: The ISSA 3,500 Sq Ft/Hr Reality Check
blocks.text: In standard commercial office environments with mixed carpet tiles and LVT corridors, a trained technician equipped with a commercial backpack vacuum and microfiber cart cleans approximately 3,500 square feet per hour. If a contractor quotes a 14,000 sq ft facility for 5x/week service but allocates only 2.0 labor hours per night (an implied 7,000 sq ft/hr pace), the crew will inevitably skip deskside high-touch disinfection, edge vacuuming, and partition glass spotting.
Step-by-Step Normalization Table: Comparing 3 Competing Proposals

Consider a representative 12,000-square-foot regional headquarters with four multi-stall restrooms, one large employee breakroom, interior conference glass partitions, and mixed carpet and vinyl plank flooring (1.05x flooring multiplier) requesting thrice-weekly service (3x/week, or 13.0 visits per month). On paper, Vendor A looks cheapest at $2,730 per month, Vendor B sits in the middle at $3,640 per month, and Vendor C appears expensive at $4,290 per month. Once normalized across identical deliverables, the financial picture shifts dramatically.

Base Rate per Cleanable Sq Ft / Visit

blocks.text: When the facility manager forces all three bids onto the same operational baseline—accounting for 13.0 monthly visits, breakroom and interior partition glass cleaning ($12 to $25 and $15 to $35 per visit respectively), paper and soap consumables ($0.012 to $0.025 per square foot per visit), and amortized quarterly floor care ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month)—all three proposals converge within an $85 monthly spread. Vendor A's apparent $1,560 monthly savings evaporated because their base price omitted breakroom appliances, interior glass, consumables, and periodic extraction.
Benchmarking Base Rates by Facility Size and Frequency

Before interrogating individual line items, verify that each bidder's cost per square foot per visit aligns with national size brackets and frequency multipliers. Smaller suites under 2,500 square feet carry higher unit rates ($0.12 to $0.20 per square foot) or trigger a mandatory minimum per-visit charge of $90 to $135 to cover technician mobilization and travel overhead. Mid-sized offices between 2,500 and 9,999 square feet typically price between $0.09 and $0.15 per square foot, while 10,000 to 24,999 square foot footprints compress down to $0.07 to $0.12 per square foot due to continuous vacuuming runs and centralized janitorial closets. Enterprise floors above 25,000 square feet command $0.05 to $0.10 per square foot.

items: Monthly or Biweekly Schedules (1.0 to 2.17 visits/month): Apply a 1.16x to 1.28x soil accumulation multiplier because heavy dust load, compacted carpet grit, and overflowing central waste bins require slower per-visit production paces.

Weekly to Twice-Weekly Schedules (4.33 to 8.66 visits/month): Twice-weekly service (1.0x baseline multiplier) serves as the standard benchmark for hybrid offices; once-weekly service adds an 8% premium (1.08x) per visit.

Three-Times-Weekly to Daily Weekday Schedules (13.0 to 21.65 visits/month): High-frequency contracts qualify for a 0.95x (3x/week) to 0.90x (5x/week) per-visit discount because soil buildup remains light and restroom restocking is predictable.

Flooring Composition Adjustments: Commercial carpet tiles represent the 1.00x baseline; VCT/LVT vinyl adds 4% (1.04x) for neutral-pH damp mopping; engineered hardwood adds 8% (1.08x) for low-moisture microfiber care; ceramic tile and grout adds 12% (1.12x) for grout scrubbing; and polished concrete reduces labor by 5% (0.95x) when serviced with walk-behind auto-scrubbers.

blocks.text: Evaluating On-Site Equipment Staging and Janitorial Closet Readiness

A common hidden variable when you compare 3 quotes is who furnishes the on-site material-handling hardware and waste receptacles. If a contractor must haul equipment up and down freight elevators from a service van every evening, you lose 20 to 30 minutes of productive cleaning time per shift. High-performing proposals specify dedicated on-site equipment staging inside your utility closet, pairing a high-capacity janitorial cart with standardized central waste and recycling stations.

During the pre-bid walkthrough, inspect whether the bidder plans to stage a multi-shelf cart like the Rubbermaid Commercial High-Capacity Janitorial Cleaning Cart (equipped with a 34-gallon zippered vinyl bag, 8-inch rear wheels, and a locking cabinet door to secure chemical concentrates away from office staff). Similarly, check how central trash removal is priced: suites outfitted with the Rubbermaid Commercial Brute 44-Gallon Vented Trash Can in copy hubs or breakrooms reduce liner pull force by 50% via molded air venting channels, cutting waste-collection labor by several minutes per floor. In narrower galley breakrooms and printer alcoves, specifying the 11-inch-wide Rubbermaid Commercial Slim Jim 23-Gallon Recycling & Waste Station with integrated bag cinches prevents torn liners and liquid spills that otherwise trigger out-of-scope spot-extraction charges.
5-Step Verification Protocol Before Signing the Winning Bid

items.name: Audit the Cleanable Square Footage Map
items.text: Subtract server closets, HVAC mechanical rooms, elevator shafts, and unfinished storage from the gross lease BOMA square footage so all three bidders multiply their unit rates against the exact same cleanable footprint.

items.name: Demand Explicit Nightly Man-Hours and Wage Floors
items.text: Require every bidder to state total nightly labor hours, supervisor inspection hours per month, and whether technicians are W-2 employees covered by statutory workers' compensation or unverified 1099 subcontractors.

items.name: Standardize the 4.33-Week Calendar Math
items.text: Verify that monthly pricing for 1x, 2x, 3x, or 5x weekly service uses 4.33 weeks per month (52 weeks divided by 12 months = 4.333) so a contractor quoting a 4-week cycle cannot bill four extra 'fifth-week' invoices per year.

items.name: Isolate Consumables and Specialty Add-Ons
items.text: Separate base labor from paper/soap restocking ($0.012-$0.025/sq ft/visit), breakroom appliance detailing ($12-$25/visit), interior glass partitions ($15-$35/visit), and amortized quarterly floor care ($0.03-$0.06/sq ft/month).

items.name: Collect Live Certificates of Insurance and OSHA Logs
items.text: Obtain a current Certificate of Insurance (COI) naming your entity as Additional Insured with at least $1M/$2M General Liability, statutory Workers' Compensation, and a $25,000 to $50,000 Janitorial Fidelity Bond, plus written OSHA HazCom Safety Data Sheet (SDS) binders.

blocks.title: Require a 30-Day Cure Clause Instead of Auto-Renewing Lock-Ins
blocks.text: Never sign a three-bid winner's boilerplate agreement containing an automatic 12-month rollover with a narrow 60-day cancellation window. Insert a standard 30-day termination-for-convenience clause and a 15-day formal cure notice tied to documented quality inspection scores.

faqs.q: Why do commercial janitorial quotes use 4.33 weeks per month instead of 4 weeks?
faqs.a: A calendar year has 52 weeks divided across 12 months, which equals 4.333 weeks per month. Four months each year contain five full workweeks. When a contractor calculates fixed monthly billing using 4.33 weeks (for example, 3x/week service equals 13.0 visits per month and 5x/week equals 21.65 visits per month), your monthly invoice stays constant year-round without surprise fifth-week surcharges.

faqs.q: What is a fair hourly bill rate when comparing three commercial cleaning bids?
faqs.a: Across most US commercial markets, standard nightly janitorial labor bills between $35 and $65 per hour, while specialty floor technicians, high-dusting crews, and emergency biohazard or post-construction work bill between $55 and $95 per hour. Any quote working out to less than $30 per billed labor hour usually signals under-allocated hours, unpaid payroll taxes, or illegal 1099 worker misclassification.

faqs.q: How do I compare quotes when one vendor includes paper and soap and another charges cost-plus?
faqs.a: Ask the all-inclusive bidder to break out their consumables allowance per square foot per visit, which typically benchmarks between $0.012 and $0.025 depending on daytime headcount and restroom traffic. Compare that flat allowance against the wholesale case price of high-capacity refills plus the competing vendor's management markup, which often runs 15% to 30% plus fuel delivery fees.

faqs.q: Should periodic carpet extraction and hard-floor buffing be included in the base quote?
faqs.a: It can be structured either way, provided all three bidders quote it identically. Best practice is requesting base nightly janitorial pricing on Line 1 and an amortized quarterly deep floor care program ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month) on Line 2, with exact contractual dates for hot-water carpet extraction and VCT scrub-and-recoat visits.
